knowledge_cards.claim: Direction/frequency decay fit is not evidence of preferred ambience or localization.
Exponentiation multiplies magnitude and group-delay fitting errors, so short filters can amplify tail error.
A sub-unity magnitude constraint is stability-oriented but is not a complete peak-safety guarantee.
SH grid and order require held-out high-frequency directional validation.
Algebraic commutation with linear transforms does not validate decoder normalization or channel conventions.
Synthetic Gaussian and simulated-SRIR validation does not establish real-room or dense-rock transfer.
Aggregate reflection-direction density can hide early-reflection timing and temporal echo-density errors.
Lower SSW distance does not establish audible motion or production usefulness.
CC BY reuse and reproducibility are separate; toolbox, CVX, seed and revision provenance remain required.
Conflicting tutorial annotations block transport of example numbers as defaults.
